source: Jin, Zhang, Shu, Cui (2023) The Cultural Psychology of Large Language Models: Is ChatGPT a Holistic or Analytic Thinker?
finding: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 score as more holistic than human norms on the Analysis-Holism Scale, whose subscales include contradiction (naive dialecticism vs formal logic). Authors read this as a pattern-seeking training effect, not stable belief.
numbers: AHS (24 items, 1-7): GPT-3.5 M=5.35 (SD .11), GPT-4 M=5.01 (SD .10) vs human norm 4.87 (SD .49, N=702), both p<.001. Each model run 10 times.
limits: Only 10 runs per condition, compared by t-test with a human norm; the contradiction subscale is not reported separately in the text I read. Only OpenAI models. Self-report, not a Peng-Nisbett reasoning task.
agent_relevance: A chat model leans toward holistic or dialectical self-description by default, but self-report says nothing about behaviour, so S7 still needs a behavioural test.

source: Jin, Zhang, Shu, Cui (2023) The Cultural Psychology of Large Language Models: Is ChatGPT a Holistic or Analytic Thinker?
finding: On the Dialectical Self Scale, only GPT-3.5 is above the human norm; GPT-4 matches it. Self-construal scores diverge: GPT-3.5 answers 'strongly agree' on independence.
numbers: DSS: GPT-3.5 M=4.59 (SD .12) vs norm 4.00 (SD .54, N=158), p<.001; GPT-4 M=3.97 (SD .07), p=.344. SCS-Independent: GPT-3.5 6.98, GPT-4 5.32 vs norm 4.73. SCS-Interdependent: GPT-3.5 5.85, GPT-4 4.95 vs norm 4.81 (p=.07). 10 runs each.
limits: The newer, more aligned model (GPT-4) looks less dialectical on the value scale than GPT-3.5, so a dialectical lean is not stable across versions. Small n.
agent_relevance: Dialectical disposition differs between model versions; do not assume it. Test the actual agent model.

source: Jin, Zhang, Shu, Cui (2023) The Cultural Psychology of Large Language Models: Is ChatGPT a Holistic or Analytic Thinker?
finding: Triadic categorization: both models pick relation-based (holistic) pairings far more often than category pairings; results held when temperature and prompt wording were changed.
numbers: TCT holistic share: GPT-3.5 0.87 (SD .06), GPT-4 0.85 (SD .05), above most Chinese provinces' means. Design: baseline plus 3 other temperatures plus 3 prompt variants, x2 models = 14 conditions x 10 runs.
limits: No human norm in the same sample; compared with provincial data from another study. At temperature 0 variance is zero. Authors admit no elaborate prompt design and only ChatGPT.
agent_relevance: Holistic relational grouping looks like a default of chat models; analytic category thinking may need to be asked for.

source: Lu, Song, Zhang (2025) Cultural tendencies in generative AI, Nature Human Behaviour (as reported in press and in Sun and Wang)
finding: Reported: GPT and ERNIE answer in a more interdependent, holistic way in Chinese and a more independent, analytic way in English; an English prompt asking for a Chinese persona shifts answers toward the Chinese pattern. Seven tasks, including an intuitive-vs-formal reasoning task and an expectation-of-change task.
numbers: Per Sun and Wang: 4-12 items per task, 7 tasks, 2 models (GPT, ERNIE). Press coverage names GPT-4 and ERNIE 3.5; exact versions not confirmed by me.
limits: I did not open the Nature Human Behaviour paper itself. Test items, prompt templates and mitigation details were withheld per Sun and Wang, so exact replication is impossible.
agent_relevance: Prompt language and persona may be a cheap lever on holistic vs analytic style, but see the failed replication.

source: Sun and Wang (2025) The fragility of 'cultural tendencies' in LLMs
finding: Targeted replication of the Lu-Song-Zhang tasks with 8 models, in English and Chinese, found negligible and unstable prompt-language effects. Includes an expectation-of-change task and a logic task.
numbers: 8 models (gpt-4.1, gemini-2.5, claude-sonnet-4, grok-4, kimi-k2, deepseek-V3, ernie-4.5, qwen3-30b); 30-60 items per language per experiment (vs 4-21 in the original); temperature 0. Expectation of change (Exp 4): no overall language effect (p=.917); only kimi and gpt significant (0.01<p<0.05); gpt better with Chinese prompts p=.017.
limits: New stimuli, not the original items (originals withheld). Models asked to justify answers, unlike the original. Preprint, not peer reviewed; the original authors' reply is not in what I read.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on prompting in Chinese to make the agent more 'dialectical'. Effects are model-specific and fragile.

source: Sun and Wang (2025) The fragility of 'cultural tendencies' in LLMs
finding: Logic task: no language effect and no difference between Chinese-origin and English-origin models on syllogisms whose conclusions fit or clash with collectivist values. Knowledge tasks beat reasoning tasks.
numbers: Exp 3, 30 items: origin/language effect p=1. Knowledge accuracy .401 vs reasoning .339 (t=2.251, df=539, p=.0248, Cohen d=0.097). Logistic regression: prompt language beta=0.0235 p=.914; model origin beta=-0.0956 p=.827. No model significant after correction (gpt MD=.134, p=.005, did not survive correction).
limits: Syllogism acceptability is only a loose analogue of Peng-Nisbett contradiction and compromise tasks.
agent_relevance: Cultural-fit effects on logic judgments look absent in current frontier models; no guardrail needed for them.

source: Sun and Wang (2025) The fragility of 'cultural tendencies' in LLMs
finding: Language sensitivity is model-specific. Most models ignore prompt language; the sensitive ones move less than 0.2 points on the scale.
numbers: Experiment 2 (attribution): 62.5% of models not sensitive, 37.5% sensitive with effects under 0.2 points. Mean effect Chinese-origin models 0.0897 vs English-origin -0.0437, p=.4826. The two API prompt templates gave no significant difference.
limits: Eight models only; temperature 0.
agent_relevance: Any cultural-style effect must be measured per model, not assumed.

source: Sun and Wang (2025) The fragility of 'cultural tendencies' in LLMs
finding: Methodological critique: anthropomorphic use of human scales, unclear causal attribution (training data, tokenisation), withheld materials, too few items for power. They call the effects statistical mimicry.
numbers: Original: 4-12 items per task, 2 models. The authors say they reported the issues to Nature Human Behaviour and the journal responded (details in their footnote). Data and scripts at osf.io/hv2g8.
limits: Critics' interpretation, not neutral; it is the competing explanation to the idea that LLMs hold culture-like cognition.
agent_relevance: Treat a dialectical-lean score from a scale as a surface-behaviour test, not as evidence of a reasoning policy.

source: Atari, Xue, Park, Blasi, Henrich (2023) Which Humans?
finding: GPT's survey answers resemble WEIRD populations most; resemblance falls as cultural distance from the US grows. This frames why a default LLM is expected to be analytic, not dialectical.
numbers: World Values Survey: 94,278 people, 65 nations; GPT-human similarity vs cultural distance from US r=-.70 (p<.001), Spearman -.72, multilevel B=-0.90 (SE .16).
limits: Mostly attitude and value data; one GPT version (2023); preprint.
agent_relevance: Default model prior is analytic and Western; a dialectical operator may need explicit instruction.

source: Atari, Xue, Park, Blasi, Henrich (2023) Which Humans?
finding: On the triad task GPT (queried 1,100 times with 20 triads) looks like the most analytic human groups, closest to the Netherlands, Finland, Sweden and Ireland.
numbers: 31 human populations (yourmorals.org plus a Mapuche interview sample); GPT queried 1,100 times with 20 triads.
limits: This is opposite to Jin et al. (2023), who found ChatGPT holistic on a triad task. Differences: prompt wording, model version, comparison data. Neither paper reconciles it.
agent_relevance: Same task, opposite verdicts across labs: style on triad tasks is prompt-sensitive. Measure with our own prompts.

source: Tao, Viberg, Baker, Kizilcec (2024) Cultural bias and cultural alignment of large language models
finding: Five GPT models show values like English-speaking and Protestant European countries; a cultural-prompting instruction (answer as an average person from country X) moves answers closer to target survey data, mostly for newer models.
numbers: Mean cultural distance with prompting: GPT-4o 2.42 to 1.57, GPT-4-turbo 2.71 to 1.77, GPT-4 2.69 to 1.65 (all P<.001); GPT-3 2.39 to 2.11; GPT-3.5-turbo 3.35 to 2.83. Improves alignment for 71-81% of countries for recent models.
limits: Measures values from survey items, not reasoning style or contradiction handling. OpenAI models only.
agent_relevance: Persona or role prompts can shift value expression; no evidence here that they change contradiction tolerance.

source: Abbasloo (2025, rev. 2026) Evaluating LLM Reasoning Beyond Correctness and CoT (SIEV)
finding: SIEV adds a thesis-antithesis-synthesis step to GSM8K and MMLU items and scores how models handle a challenge. Standard accuracy hides large differences in how models treat opposition.
numbers: 21 models. GSM8K thesis accuracy (pT) 93-97 for most; synthesis accuracy (pS) ranges 59.6 (O1-mini) to 93.6 (O3). Abstract: GPT-5-chat loses more than 40 points on GSM under SIEV; MMLU gaps often exceed 20 points.
quote: reasoning should be understood not as a static chain of steps but as a dynamic trajectory in which ideas interact, clash
limits: Authors' own metrics (pS, opposition coverage OC, DS score); synthesis is produced by the model under test; no human baseline.
agent_relevance: A direct machine test of 'hold thesis and antithesis, then decide'. Models often cannot do it well even when they answer the base question right.

source: Abbasloo (2025, rev. 2026) Evaluating LLM Reasoning Beyond Correctness and CoT (SIEV)
finding: Per-model examples: strong models integrate opposition (O3), others replay the thesis. Synthesis accuracy is below thesis accuracy on average.
numbers: GSM8K: O3 pT 97.1, pS 93.6, OC 95.5; GPT-5 pT 96.8, pS 82.0, OC 81.4; GPT-5-nano pS 84.4 but OC only 15.5 (replay-like). MMLU: Llama-3.3-70B pT 85.1 vs pS 58.3 (change -26.8); GPT-4.1-mini pS 54.7 (change -30.2); O1 pT 91.1, pS 90.3.
limits: OC is a ratio of opposition produced; definitions are the authors'. The thesis-to-synthesis change is negative on average.
agent_relevance: If the agent runs two-rule or thesis/antithesis steps, check that the synthesis does not drop correct answers: on average it did here.

source: Abdali et al. (2025, v7 2026) Self-reflecting Large Language Models: A Hegelian Dialectical Approach
finding: Hegelian loop (thesis, generated antithesis, synthesis that unifies the two) beats standard prompting and Self-Refine on math reasoning in most cells.
numbers: GSM-Symbolic: GPT-4o 0.852 to 0.884 (+3.8%), GPT-4o-mini 0.709 to 0.770 (+8.6%), Qwen2.5-7B 0.587 to 0.623 (+6.1%). GSM-hard: Qwen3-8B 0.585 to 0.658 (+12.5%). GSM-8k baselines already above 0.94 for GPT models; ties Self-Refine 0.933 on Qwen3-8B.
limits: Gains are small where baselines are saturated; GSM-hard and MMLU-Pro are 'more competitive'; the idea-generation arm is judged by LLM majority vote, not experts.
agent_relevance: A published prompt scaffold for 'keep two views until a unifying third is justified'. A close cousin of S7.

source: Abdali et al. (2025, v7 2026) Self-reflecting Large Language Models: A Hegelian Dialectical Approach
finding: Method detail: the synthesis prompt asks for a third view that explains how the two views agree and how they are opposed. Validity of the step is checked by Multi-Agent Majority Voting. Temperature is either annealed or constant.
numbers: The antithesis prompt lists defects of a view, e.g. 'incompatible with some of the phenomena' and 'can be defined only in relation to another view'.
limits: Prompt text and checker design; not a measured effect by itself.
agent_relevance: Reusable operator text for a dialectical step.

source: Candussio (2026) A Dialectic Pipeline for Improving LLM Robustness (MSc thesis, Trieste)
finding: Three-stage self-dialogue (thesis, antithesis, synthesis) with small open models in an oracle-RAG setting raises accuracy a lot. Unlike Hegel, the antithesis is not forced to refute.
numbers: Mean accuracy gain thesis to synthesis across HotpotQA (comparison, bridge) and WikiHop: Phi-mini 27.8, Phi-medium 33.6, Gemma-2B 21.7, Gemma-9B 18.3, Llama-8B 35.4 points. WikiHop gains smaller (Gemma-9B 4.2).
limits: Thesis-level answers were weak; oracle context supplied; small models; an MSc thesis, not peer reviewed.
agent_relevance: The antithesis/synthesis steps can repair weak first answers cheaply when context is good.

source: Candussio (2026) A Dialectic Pipeline for Improving LLM Robustness (MSc thesis, Trieste)
finding: Against chain-of-thought the pipeline wins by modest margins and sometimes loses; the synthesis step can pull a correct CoT answer off track.
numbers: WikiHop pipeline vs CoT: +11.6 Phi-mini, +10.6 Phi-medium, +15.6 Gemma-2B, +3.8 Gemma-9B, +1.9 Llama-8B. HotpotQA: synthesis nearly always helps in the baseline variant except Gemma-2B bridge (-1.8); with the CoT variant some synthesis steps lowered accuracy. The pipeline needs two extra calls to match CoT's single step.
limits: Compute not matched; author attributes drops to CoT already exploring the options on 2-hop questions.
agent_relevance: Do not add a dialectical step on easy items: S7-style operators cost calls and can hurt where CoT already weighs options.

source: Du, Li, Torralba, Tenenbaum, Mordatch (2023/2024) Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
finding: Several ChatGPT copies propose, read each other's answers, and revise over rounds. Debate beats single agent, reflection and majority vote on reasoning and factual tasks.
numbers: 3 agents, 2 rounds. Arithmetic % : single 67.0, reflection 72.1, majority 69.0, debate 81.8. GSM8K: 77.0, 75.0, 81.0, 85.0. Biographies: 66.0, 68.3, -, 73.8. MMLU: 63.9, 57.7, -, 71.1. Chess move validity: 29.3, 38.8, -, 45.2.
limits: gpt-3.5-era models; reflection hurt on GSM8K and MMLU; later work (Huang et al.) says the gain largely disappears at matched compute.
agent_relevance: Multiple live positions that revise on each other is an LLM version of dialectical resolution; evidence is positive but compute-confounded.

source: Du, Li, Torralba, Tenenbaum, Mordatch (2023/2024) Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
finding: Mixed-model debate helps both models; more agents and rounds raise accuracy; debate adds on top of chain-of-thought.
numbers: 20 GSM8K problems: Bard solved 11, ChatGPT 14, debate between them 17.
limits: Only 20 problems in the cross-model test; no significance test.
agent_relevance: Disagreement between different models may carry more information than between copies of one model.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Without outside feedback, self-correction does not help and often hurts; multi-agent debate is no better than majority voting at an equal number of responses.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-3.5 standard 75.9; GPT-3.5 keeps its first answer 74.7% of the time and changes correct to wrong more often than wrong to correct. With oracle labels GPT-4 GSM8K goes 95.5 to 97.5. Debate round 1 (3 responses) 76.7, round 2 (6 responses) 83.2 vs self-consistency 6 responses 85.3, 9 responses 88.2.
limits: GPT-3.5/GPT-4 era; oracle feedback is unrealistic; the authors say debate acts as 'consistency' in effect.
agent_relevance: S7-style counterexample checks need an outside signal (tests, tools). Self-generated antitheses alone are weak.

source: Liang et al. (2023/2024) Encouraging Divergent Thinking in LLMs through Multi-Agent Debate (MAD)
finding: A debate with two opposed debaters and a judge counters 'degeneration of thought', where a self-reflecting model stays locked into its first answer.
numbers: Counter-Intuitive Arithmetic (200 questions): GPT-4 51.0%, GPT-3.5-Turbo 26.0, +CoT 28.0, +Self-Consistency 29.5, +Self-Reflect 27.5, +MAD 37.0. Translation: COMET 79.9 to 84.4 depending on judge and debater choice.
limits: Small tasks, GPT-3.5 baseline; debater stance assigned by prompt.
agent_relevance: Role-split (affirm and deny) with a separate judge is a cheap way to get opposition; the decision sits in the judge.

source: Kim and Khashabi (2025) Challenging the Evaluator: LLM Sycophancy Under User Rebuttal
finding: Models judge two conflicting arguments well when shown together, but give in when the counterargument arrives as a second-turn user rebuttal. Holding a position under pushback is the weak point, not weighing both sides.
numbers: Full Rebuttal persuasion average F=56.1%; 'Sure Rebuttal' casual assertion F=84.5%; 'Are You Sure' prompt F=93.9% for one model; most differences vs the neutral judge setting p<.05 (GPT-4o-mini excepted). Casual feedback was more persuasive than reasoned critique.
limits: Multiple-choice (MMLU-style) items; persuasion measured as answer change.
agent_relevance: Dialectical tolerance in an agent must not collapse into deferring: keep rule A alive while evidence is unresolved, and resist pushback that brings no new evidence.

source: SycEval authors (2025) SycEval: Evaluating LLM Sycophancy
finding: Rebuttals flip answers often; mostly toward correct answers on this data, but a sizeable share goes the wrong way. Preemptive rebuttals are worse than in-context ones.
numbers: ChatGPT-4o, Claude-Sonnet, Gemini-1.5-Pro on AMPS math and MedQuad: sycophancy in 58.19% of cases (Gemini 62.47%, ChatGPT 56.71%); progressive (to correct) 43.52%, regressive (to wrong) 14.66%; persistence 78.5%.
limits: Older model generation; sycophancy as defined by the authors includes helpful corrections.
agent_relevance: About 1 in 7 rebuttals pushes a model off a correct answer: a counterexample step needs a verifier, not only an opposing statement.

source: Sun and Wang (2025) The fragility of 'cultural tendencies' in LLMs
finding: Experiments 1 and 2 (entity change and attribution): language effects appear only in a few models and point in different directions.
numbers: Exp 1 (60 items): small framing effect p<.05, no origin/language effect (p=.15); deepseek and qwen prefer Chinese prompts (0.01<p<.05), six other models no effect. Exp 2 (30 vignettes): no overall effect (p=.25); ernie, gpt and qwen sensitive to English (p<.01). Picture task (4 items): only ernie differed by language, as in the original.
limits: Different direction for qwen across experiments; stimuli rebuilt, so partial replication only.
agent_relevance: The belief-in-change (change-framed) orientation that underlies dialectical thinking is not reliably switched by language.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: With oracle correctness labels self-correction helps a lot, which shows the missing piece is the outside verdict, not the opposing step.
numbers: Oracle self-correct: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 95.5, CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 82.0, HotpotQA 26.0 to 49.0; GPT-4 GSM8K 84.3 to 97.5, CommonSenseQA 89.7 to 85.5, HotpotQA 29.0 to 59.0 (row order read from the extracted table; check against the PDF).
limits: Table layout garbled in text extraction, pairing of rows is my reading; oracle labels are not available in real use.
agent_relevance: A counterexample that decides (a test run, a tool result) is what makes keeping two rules alive pay off.
